sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档关于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店当DJ的黑胶唱片时代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去上班，把DJ台变成了一个充满50年历史精美文物的流动博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today, six months ago, Donald Trump addressed the possibility that North Korean missiles could reach the United States.
sentences.zh: 今天，六个月前，唐纳德·特朗普谈到了朝鲜导弹可能触及美国的可能性。

sentences.en: It won't happen, he said.
sentences.zh: 他说，这不会发生。

sentences.en: How the U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国是如何

sentences.en: underestimated North Korea.
sentences.zh: 低估朝鲜的。

sentences.en: And few states have benefited so dramatically from the expansion of Medicaid as Kentucky.
sentences.zh: 很少有州像肯塔基州这样，从医疗补助计划（Medicaid）的扩张中获益如此巨大。

sentences.en: So why is the man leading the charge to roll it back, a senator from Kentucky?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么带头要求撤销该计划的人，偏偏是一位来自肯塔基州的参议员呢？

sentences.en: It's Thursday, July 6th.
sentences.zh: 今天是7月6日，星期四。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: David.
sentences.zh: 大卫。

sentences.en: Hey, how are you?
sentences.zh: 嘿，你好吗？

sentences.en: Hey, it's Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: Good to talk to you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴和你通话。

sentences.en: Where are you exactly?
sentences.zh: 你现在具体在哪里？

sentences.en: I am in the United Lounge at New York Airport.
sentences.zh: 我在纽约机场的联合航空贵宾室。

sentences.en: On your way to?
sentences.zh: 正要去哪儿？

sentences.en: To Homburg for the G20 summit.
sentences.zh: 去汉堡参加G20峰会。

sentences.en: We've got a bunch of questions to get through.
sentences.zh: 我们有一堆问题要讨论。

sentences.en: This is pretty interesting stuff.
sentences.zh: 这些内容相当有趣。

sentences.en: Although I'm now wondering about this small child right near David.
sentences.zh: 虽然我现在对大卫身边那个小孩感到好奇。

sentences.en: You're wondering about what?
sentences.zh: 你对什么感到好奇？

sentences.en: About the proximity of a small child near you in the United Club?
sentences.zh: 对联合航空贵宾室里那个离你很近的小孩吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, well...
sentences.zh: 是啊，那个……

sentences.en: Any way to get that kid on a flight to Germany right now?
sentences.zh: 有什么办法能让那孩子现在就坐上飞往德国的航班吗？

sentences.en: I think the child's father just walked away with us.
sentences.zh: 我想那孩子的父亲刚刚和我们走开了。

sentences.en: I'll come back with some food in a minute.
sentences.zh: 我一会儿带点吃的回来。

sentences.en: All right, let's jump in.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们开始吧。

sentences.en: David Sanger, what did North Korea accomplish with this missile test?
sentences.zh: 大卫·桑格，朝鲜这次导弹试验达成了什么目的？

sentences.en: They accomplished something that they've been talking about for years, which was a missile that could plausibly reach American shores, the American mainland.
sentences.zh: 他们达成了一项谈论多年的目标，即拥有一种理论上可以触及美国海岸、触及美国本土的导弹。

sentences.en: But they did it in a very ingenious way, something they've been doing in recent months, which is they shot it way up into outer space, 1,700 miles up,
sentences.zh: 但他们采取了一种非常巧妙的方式，这也是他们近几个月来一直在做的事，那就是将导弹高高射入外太空，高度达到1700英里，

sentences.en: and had it come down at a very steep parabola, just as an intercontinental ballistic missile would, in a way that would make it very hard for the United States to shoot down.
sentences.zh: 然后让它以非常陡峭的抛物线落下，就像洲际弹道导弹那样，这种方式会让美国很难将其拦截。

sentences.en: David, how far ahead is North Korea of where we thought North Korea was, based on the distance that this missile traveled?
sentences.zh: 大卫，根据这次导弹飞行的距离来看，朝鲜的进度比我们预想的领先了多少？

sentences.en: In other words, how much of a surprise was this?
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这有多出人意料？

sentences.en: The surprise here is all in the timing, not in the accomplishment.
sentences.zh: 这次的意外全在于时机，而不在于成就本身。

sentences.en: The United States has consistently underestimated the speed at which North Korea would move up the ladder of its technology.
sentences.zh: 美国一直低估了朝鲜在技术阶梯上攀升的速度。

sentences.en: I think there's going to be a lot of study about why the United States got this wrong.
sentences.zh: 我想会有很多人研究美国为什么会判断失误。

sentences.en: You know, we all have grown up on one giant intelligence failure, Iraq, where the intelligence community overestimated Saddam Hussein's ability to build a nuclear weapon
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们都是在一次巨大的情报失败中长大的，那就是伊拉克战争，当时情报界高估了萨达姆·侯赛因制造核武器的能力，

sentences.en: and perhaps to deliver it.
sentences.zh: 以及可能投送核武器的能力。

sentences.en: What we forget in the middle of that is that there have been many nuclear and missile intelligence failures,
sentences.zh: 我们在那件事中忽略的是，历史上还有过许多核武器和导弹方面的情报失误，

sentences.en: but almost all of the other ones, pre-Iraq, went in the other direction, that we underestimated the country's capability.
sentences.zh: 但几乎所有伊拉克战争之前的失误，方向都恰恰相反，即我们低估了这些国家的能力。

sentences.en: So we underestimated how quickly the Soviets would be able to do this and set off their own nuclear weapon in 1949.
sentences.zh: 所以我们低估了苏联在1949年能够多快做到这一点并引爆他们自己的核武器。

sentences.en: We underestimated how long it would take the Chinese in the early 60s.
sentences.zh: 我们低估了中国在60年代初需要多长时间。

sentences.en: We underestimated how long it would take the Indians in the 70s and the Pakistanis in the 80s.
sentences.zh: 我们低估了印度在70年代和巴基斯坦在80年代所需的时间。

sentences.en: But we forget that history because the most recent mistake we've made was in the other direction.
sentences.zh: 但我们忘记了那段历史，因为我们最近一次犯的错误方向正好相反。

sentences.en: David, why do you think we're so prone to underestimating foreign countries' nuclear capabilities?
sentences.zh: 大卫，你认为我们为什么总是倾向于低估外国的核能力？

sentences.en: Because nothing is more secret within a country than how they are doing in their missile and their nuclear technology and in merging those two technologies.
sentences.zh: 因为在一个国家内部，没有什么比他们在导弹和核技术方面的发展，以及如何将这两种技术融合在一起更机密的了。

sentences.en: They keep this very well hidden, and North Korea is a particularly hard target.
sentences.zh: 他们把这些隐藏得非常好，而朝鲜是一个特别难对付的目标。

sentences.en: What happens now?
sentences.zh: 现在会发生什么？

sentences.en: What does the United States do, given this advancement in the North Korean technology?
sentences.zh: 鉴于朝鲜在技术上的这一进步，美国会怎么做？

sentences.en: Well, Michael, as we've discussed before, North Korea is the land of lousy options, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，迈克尔，正如我们之前讨论过的，朝鲜是一个充满糟糕选择的地方，对吧？

sentences.en: Every incremental advance that North Koreans have made have left the president to make a really tough decision.
sentences.zh: 朝鲜人每一次渐进式的进步，都让总统不得不做出一个非常艰难的决定。

sentences.en: And that decision is, what's the worst thing that you could do here?
sentences.zh: 而那个决定就是，你能做的最糟糕的事情是什么？

sentences.en: Live with this incremental improvement or take a set of actions that could end up in a retaliation against Seoul, a city of 10 million people, a close U.S.
sentences.zh: 是忍受这种渐进式的改善，还是采取一系列可能导致针对首尔——一个拥有1000万人口的美国盟友城市，以及周边郊区更多居民——进行报复的行动？

sentences.en: ally, many more people living in the immediate suburbs of that.
sentences.zh: （续上句）

sentences.en: And everybody has determined, in the end, that the cost isn't worth the benefit.
sentences.zh: 最终每个人都认定，代价大于收益。

sentences.en: Well, Kim Jong-un's figured this out as well.
sentences.zh: 嗯，金正恩也看透了这一点。

sentences.en: And so he has come to the determination that the threats are all pretty empty,
sentences.zh: 所以他得出了一个结论，认为这些威胁都相当空洞，

sentences.en: that the United States, in the end, isn't going to take military action against him because they're afraid of the consequences,
sentences.zh: 认为美国最终不会对他采取军事行动，因为他们害怕后果，

sentences.en: that the Chinese, in the end, aren't going to cut off his oil because they're afraid of chaos on their border if North Korea collapses.
sentences.zh: 认为中国最终不会切断他的石油供应，因为他们害怕如果朝鲜崩溃，边境会陷入混乱。

sentences.en: So he has played a very weak hand incredibly well.
sentences.zh: 所以他把一手烂牌打得极其出色。

sentences.en: Michael, hold on a second.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，等一下。

sentences.en: I'm going to walk away from the returning kids here.
sentences.zh: 我要离开这些回来的孩子们了。

sentences.en: We'll see how we do.
sentences.zh: 看看效果如何。

sentences.en: Okay, tell me how the reception is here.
sentences.zh: 好的，告诉我这里的信号怎么样。

sentences.en: Good?
sentences.zh: 好吗？

sentences.en: Good, good, good, yep.
sentences.zh: 好，好，好，是的。

sentences.en: Good.
sentences.zh: 好。

sentences.en: And David, we've been talking around this a little bit, but if I'm a listener, this is probably my number one question.
sentences.zh: 大卫，我们一直在绕着这个问题谈，但如果我是听众，这可能是我最关心的问题。

sentences.en: How much do we need to worry now that a nuclear weapon will be launched from North Korea to the United States?
sentences.zh: 现在我们有多大必要担心朝鲜会向美国发射核武器？

sentences.en: I don't think you need to worry that one day Kim Jong-un is going to wake up and say,
sentences.zh: 我不认为你需要担心有一天金正恩会醒来说，

sentences.en: I'm going to start a nuclear war with the United States.
sentences.zh: 我要对美国发动核战争。

sentences.en: He knows what would happen in the ensuing 45 minutes to an hour.
sentences.zh: 他知道接下来的45分钟到一个小时内会发生什么。

sentences.en: And remember, it's his regime he wants to protect.
sentences.zh: 记住，他想要保护的是他自己的政权。

sentences.en: My biggest concern, Michael, actually isn't a North Korea that is aggressively going after the United States.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，我最大的担忧其实不是朝鲜会主动攻击美国。

sentences.en: It's a North Korea in which there's a small conflict that turns to a larger one and goes nuclear, or a North Korea that's in collapse.
sentences.zh: 而是朝鲜发生小规模冲突演变成大规模冲突并动用核武器，或者朝鲜陷入崩溃。

sentences.en: And somebody loyal to Kim Jong-un who's grown up in that propaganda environment for decades
sentences.zh: 而某个忠于金正恩、在那种宣传环境中成长了几十年的人，

sentences.en: suddenly is concerned that the whole country is going down in flames and he's going to take someone out with it.
sentences.zh: 突然担心整个国家要完蛋了，于是决定拉人垫背。

sentences.en: And hits the launch button.
sentences.zh: 然后按下了发射按钮。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We didn't really worry about this for the Soviet Union because while we were concerned about the nuclear arms race
sentences.zh: 我们并没有真正担心过苏联，因为虽然我们担心核军备竞赛，

sentences.en: and we were concerned about being destroyed, we fundamentally believe they had good control over their nuclear weapons.
sentences.zh: 也担心被摧毁，但我们从根本上相信他们对自己的核武器有很好的控制。

sentences.en: And even India and Pakistan, we were more worried about them going after each other than going after us.
sentences.zh: 即使是印度和巴基斯坦，我们担心的也是他们互相攻击，而不是攻击我们。

sentences.en: But in North Korea's case, we don't understand who's in control of their weapons.
sentences.zh: 但在朝鲜的问题上，我们不了解是谁在控制他们的武器。

sentences.en: So that's my biggest worry.
sentences.zh: 所以这是我最大的担忧。

sentences.en: My biggest worry is what goes wrong if the place appears to be in mid-collapse.
sentences.zh: 我最大的担忧是，如果这个国家看起来处于崩溃边缘，会发生什么差错。

sentences.en: David, thank you very much and have a safe trip to Germany and we'll talk to you later.
sentences.zh: 大卫，非常感谢你，祝你去德国的旅途平安，我们稍后再聊。

sentences.en: Thanks very much, Michael.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢，迈克尔。

sentences.en: Okay, bye.
sentences.zh: 好的，再见。

sentences.en: On Wednesday, in response to North Korea's missile test, the United States and South Korea conducted a joint military exercise
sentences.zh: 周三，为了回应朝鲜的导弹试验，美国和韩国进行了联合军事演习，

sentences.en: that involved firing an undisclosed number of ballistic missiles into the sea.
sentences.zh: 其中包括向海中发射了数量不详的弹道导弹。

sentences.en: After the test, the top American commander in South Korea, General Vincent Brooks, said that, quote, self-restraint is all that is keeping the U.S.
sentences.zh: 试验结束后，美国驻韩最高指挥官文森特·布鲁克斯将军表示，引用他的话，克制是目前阻止美韩与朝鲜开战的唯一因素。

sentences.en: and South Korea from going to war with the North.
sentences.zh: （续上句）

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《交易手册》（DealBook）报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市的《交易手册》峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的领导人，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼等等。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无保留、未经修饰的对话实况。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将在11月18日通过NYTimes.com直播部分采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻报道一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: Senate Republicans have a particularly complicated challenge facing them as they try to pass their health care bill.
sentences.zh: 共和党参议员在试图通过医改法案时，面临着一项特别复杂的挑战。

sentences.en: After years of promising to repeal Obamacare, many constituents back in their home states have come to depend on it, like it or not.
sentences.zh: 在承诺废除奥巴马医改多年后，许多选民在各自的州已经开始依赖它，无论他们是否喜欢。

sentences.en: Nowhere is that tension and contradiction more apparent than in Kentucky, with its two Republican senators and its relationship to Medicaid.
sentences.zh: 这种紧张和矛盾在肯塔基州表现得最为明显，该州有两位共和党参议员，且与医疗补助计划有着密切关系。

sentences.en: You know, Kentucky is really a showpiece for the expansion of Medicaid under Obamacare.
sentences.zh: 你知道，肯塔基州确实是奥巴马医改下医疗补助计划扩张的样板。

sentences.en: Cheryl Stolberg has been reporting from Kentucky.
sentences.zh: 谢丽尔·斯托尔伯格一直在肯塔基州进行报道。

sentences.en: Right now, one in three Kentuckians, nearly one in three, is on Medicaid.
sentences.zh: 目前，三分之一的肯塔基人，几乎是三分之一，都在享受医疗补助。

sentences.en: And of those, about a third get Medicaid through the expansion.
sentences.zh: 而在这些人中，约有三分之一是通过扩张计划获得医疗补助的。

sentences.en: And you know, Michael, in some poor eastern Kentucky, Appalachia counties, more than 60% of people are on Medicaid.
sentences.zh: 而且你知道，迈克尔，在肯塔基州一些贫困的阿巴拉契亚县，超过60%的人都在享受医疗补助。

sentences.en: Now, Kentucky also is struggling with the opioid epidemic.
sentences.zh: 现在，肯塔基州也在与阿片类药物流行作斗争。

sentences.en: And you've got to remember, Kentucky is a very poor state.
sentences.zh: 你必须记住，肯塔基州是一个非常贫穷的州。

sentences.en: It's a state that has been decimated.
sentences.zh: 这是一个遭受重创的州。

sentences.en: And job losses have just been abysmal, crushing, as a result of the coal downturn.
sentences.zh: 由于煤炭行业的衰退，失业情况简直惨不忍睹，令人窒息。

sentences.en: So all these things come together to make Kentucky kind of a crucible for this debate.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些因素加在一起，使肯塔基州成为了这场辩论的熔炉。

sentences.en: So that sounds like a large number of people who got on Medicaid through the Affordable Care Act.
sentences.zh: 听起来有很多人是通过《平价医疗法案》获得医疗补助的。

sentences.en: Do you know how many it is?
sentences.zh: 你知道具体有多少人吗？

sentences.en: Roughly 400,000.
sentences.zh: 大约40万。

sentences.en: Maybe a little bit less than 400,000.
sentences.zh: 可能比40万少一点点。

sentences.en: And how has the Medicaid expansion of the Affordable Care Act worked in Kentucky?
sentences.zh: 那么《平价医疗法案》的医疗补助扩张在肯塔基州是如何运作的呢？

sentences.en: What does it look like?
sentences.zh: 它是什么样子的？

sentences.en: Well, I guess I might say it looks like a woman I met called Kathy Collins.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想我可能会说，它看起来就像我遇到的一位名叫凯西·柯林斯的女士。

sentences.en: Hello?
sentences.zh: 喂？

sentences.en: Hi, is this Kathy?
sentences.zh: 你好，是凯西吗？

sentences.en: Yes, it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，我是。

sentences.en: Hey, Kathy, it's Michael Barbaro from The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 嘿，凯西，我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: I'm good.
sentences.zh: 我很好。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你呢？

sentences.en: Good.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.en: I'm really grateful to you for spending some time with us.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你花时间接受我们的采访。

sentences.en: So thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: You're welcome.
sentences.zh: 不客气。

sentences.en: And my colleague, Cheryl Stolberg, sends her best, too.
sentences.zh: 我的同事谢丽尔·斯托尔伯格也向你问好。

sentences.en: She gave me your phone number.
sentences.zh: 是她给了我你的电话号码。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Kathy was a patient at a hospital in Whitesburg, Kentucky, a tiny little city in eastern Kentucky.
sentences.zh: 凯西曾是肯塔基州怀茨堡一家医院的病人，那是一个位于肯塔基州东部的小城市。

sentences.en: And she has lupus, an autoimmune disease.
sentences.zh: 她患有狼疮，这是一种自身免疫性疾病。

sentences.en: Well, it took them several years to diagnose it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们花了几年时间才诊断出来。

sentences.en: The proper diagnosis came in 2010, but I got sick in 2005.
sentences.zh: 确诊是在2010年，但我2005年就病了。

sentences.en: And how did you know you were sick?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么知道自己生病的？

sentences.en: What are the symptoms?
sentences.zh: 有什么症状？

sentences.en: What are the symptoms of lupus?
sentences.zh: 狼疮的症状是什么？

sentences.en: I broke out in large welts.
sentences.zh: 我身上长出了大片的风团。

sentences.en: My joints started swell everywhere.
sentences.zh: 我的关节开始到处肿胀。

sentences.en: It's very painful.
sentences.zh: 这非常痛苦。

sentences.en: Did you have health insurance when you were diagnosed with lupus?
sentences.zh: 你被诊断出患有狼疮时有医疗保险吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: And so how did you get health insurance?
sentences.zh: 那你后来是怎么获得医疗保险的？

sentences.en: And how were you treated?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么接受治疗的？

sentences.en: Let's see.
sentences.zh: 让我想想。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And that's expensive.
sentences.zh: 而且那很贵。

sentences.en: If it hadn't been for my dad or my family.
sentences.zh: 如果不是因为我父亲或我的家人。

sentences.en: And then what happened?
sentences.zh: 然后发生了什么？

sentences.en: It sounds like you then got to medicate.
sentences.zh: 听起来你后来得以用药了。

sentences.en: How did that work?
sentences.zh: 那是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: Why were you surprised?
sentences.zh: 你为什么会感到惊讶？

sentences.en: I didn't think I'd be approved.
sentences.zh: 我没想过我会获批。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: Do you have a job?
sentences.zh: 你有工作吗？

sentences.en: Do you have income?
sentences.zh: 你有收入吗？

sentences.en: No, sir.
sentences.zh: 没有，先生。

sentences.en: I'm disabled.
sentences.zh: 我是残疾人。

sentences.en: What does your income look like?
sentences.zh: 你的收入情况如何？

sentences.en: It sounds like you have been ill for long enough that you have not been able to work.
sentences.zh: 听起来你生病的时间已经长到无法工作了。

sentences.en: So what are your sources of income?
sentences.zh: 那么你的收入来源是什么？

sentences.en: Security.
sentences.zh: 社会保障金。

sentences.en: I would be shocked to know.
sentences.zh: 如果我知道具体金额，我会很震惊的。

sentences.en: Meaning it's not that much?
sentences.zh: 意思是没多少钱？

sentences.en: No, it's not.
sentences.zh: 不，确实不多。

sentences.en: I couldn't pay rent and utilities and buy groceries on what I draw.
sentences.zh: 靠我领的那点钱，我根本付不起房租、水电费，也买不起生活用品。

sentences.en: There's no way.
sentences.zh: 根本不可能。

sentences.en: I'm actually my independence.
sentences.zh: 我其实是靠我的独立性（支撑着）。

sentences.en: When I got sick and had to go on disability.
sentences.zh: 当我生病不得不申请残疾救济时。

sentences.en: And that is why you qualified for Medicaid under the Affordable Care Act?
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么你根据《平价医疗法案》获得了医疗补助计划（Medicaid）的资格？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And how would you say that that Medicaid has been for you?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这个医疗补助计划对你来说怎么样？

sentences.en: It's been a lot.
sentences.zh: 帮助很大。

sentences.en: So I want to ask you just a little bit about politics because of the health care debate that's going on in this country.
sentences.zh: 所以我想问你一点关于政治的问题，因为这个国家正在进行医疗保健辩论。

sentences.en: Have you voted for your two senators, Senator Mitch McConnell and Senator Rand Paul?
sentences.zh: 你投票支持过你的两位参议员，米奇·麦康奈尔参议员和兰德·保罗参议员吗？

sentences.en: So, Cheryl, I want to talk about Kentucky's senators who are at the center of this debate over health care.
sentences.zh: 那么，谢丽尔，我想谈谈肯塔基州的参议员，他们正处于这场医疗保健辩论的中心。

sentences.en: What are their positions towards Medicaid and the Affordable Care Act?
sentences.zh: 他们对医疗补助计划和《平价医疗法案》持什么立场？

sentences.en: Senator Mitch McConnell is the Republican leader of the Senate.
sentences.zh: 米奇·麦康奈尔参议员是参议院的共和党领袖。

sentences.en: And right now it's his job to try to push through a repeal of the Affordable Care Act.
sentences.zh: 而现在他的工作是试图推动废除《平价医疗法案》。

sentences.en: The status quo is simply unsustainable.
sentences.zh: 现状根本无法持续。

sentences.en: It'll be dealt with in one of two ways.
sentences.zh: 它将通过两种方式之一来解决。

sentences.en: Either Republicans will agree and change the status quo.
sentences.zh: 要么共和党人达成一致并改变现状。

sentences.en: Or the markets will continue to collapse.
sentences.zh: 要么市场将继续崩溃。

sentences.en: And under the Senate bill, the bill would undo much of the Medicaid expansion.
sentences.zh: 根据参议院的法案，该法案将撤销大部分医疗补助计划的扩张。

sentences.en: We need to come up with a solution.
sentences.zh: 我们需要拿出一个解决方案。

sentences.en: The American people elected us to do that.
sentences.zh: 美国人民选我们出来就是为了做这件事。

sentences.en: And we're working hard to get there.
sentences.zh: 我们正在努力实现这一目标。

sentences.en: He's kind of the wrangler, right?
sentences.zh: 他算是那个协调者，对吧？

sentences.en: He's got to pull together both sides of his party.
sentences.zh: 他必须把党内两派团结起来。

sentences.en: The moderates who are worried that rolling this back too much is going to hurt people in their state.
sentences.zh: 温和派担心撤回太多会伤害他们州的人民。

sentences.en: And the conservatives who are worried that the Senate bill doesn't do enough to cut costs.
sentences.zh: 而保守派则担心参议院的法案在削减成本方面做得不够。

sentences.en: It is a conundrum.
sentences.zh: 这是一个难题。

sentences.en: That's why we should vote on the one thing that we all agreed on.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们应该就我们都同意的那一件事进行投票。

sentences.en: About a year ago, we voted on clean repeal.
sentences.zh: 大约一年前，我们投票支持了彻底废除。

sentences.en: Now let's go to Senator No.
sentences.zh: 现在让我们来看看“不”先生。

sentences.en: 2, the leader of the pack among those conservative critics, Senator Rand Paul.
sentences.zh: 排名第二，那些保守派批评者中的领头羊，兰德·保罗参议员。

sentences.en: He might be called a free market conservative.
sentences.zh: 他可能被称为自由市场保守派。

sentences.en: He's a libertarian.
sentences.zh: 他是一位自由意志主义者。

sentences.en: And he wants even deeper cuts than those that would be made in the bill Senator McConnell is shepherding and trying to get Republican agreement on.
sentences.zh: 他想要的削减力度甚至比麦康奈尔参议员正在引导并试图获得共和党人同意的法案中的削减还要大。

sentences.en: The current Medicaid is unfunded.
sentences.zh: 目前的医疗补助计划是没有资金支持的。

sentences.en: And then we're going to add new entitlement programs to that.
sentences.zh: 然后我们还要在上面增加新的福利项目。

sentences.en: If you really want to have Medicaid for everyone in all these states, you should be honest with the people.
sentences.zh: 如果你真的想让所有这些州的所有人都享有医疗补助，你应该对人民诚实。

sentences.en: And you should double or triple the state income tax and double or triple the sales tax.
sentences.zh: 你应该将州所得税和销售税提高一倍或两倍。

sentences.en: Now I'm not for that, but that's what it would take if you were honeSt.
sentences.zh: 我并不支持那样，但如果你诚实的话，这就是所需要的代价。

sentences.en: Instead, we say, oh, federal government's going to pay for it.
sentences.zh: 相反，我们说，哦，联邦政府会买单。

sentences.en: Federal government has no money.
sentences.zh: 联邦政府没钱。

sentences.en: We borrow a million dollars a minute, so it's just dishonest accounting.
sentences.zh: 我们每分钟借一百万美元，所以这只是不诚实的会计手段。

sentences.en: I think what they represent is sort of the Republican Party fighting with itself.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们所代表的是共和党内部的自我斗争。

sentences.en: It's sort of got this internal battle going on, and they don't seem to know quite how to resolve it.
sentences.zh: 它似乎正在进行一场内部战斗，他们似乎不知道该如何解决。

sentences.en: It's why Senator McConnell had to pull the health care bill from the Senate floor, because he didn't have the votes to pass it.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么麦康奈尔参议员不得不从参议院撤回医疗保健法案，因为他没有足够的票数通过它。

sentences.en: So I guess we have to ask this inevitable question here.
sentences.zh: 所以我猜我们必须在这里问一个不可避免的问题。

sentences.en: If, as the numbers you describe suggest, the expansion of Medicaid in Kentucky has been numerically a success,
sentences.zh: 如果正如你描述的数据所暗示的那样，肯塔基州医疗补助计划的扩张在数字上是成功的，

sentences.en: and so many people who didn't have insurance now get their insurance through Medicaid in Kentucky under the Affordable Care Act,
sentences.zh: 而且许多以前没有保险的人现在通过《平价医疗法案》在肯塔基州获得了医疗补助，

sentences.en: why are the senior elected officials in the state trying to roll that back?
sentences.zh: 为什么该州的高级民选官员试图撤回它？

sentences.en: How does that work?
sentences.zh: 那是怎么运作的？

sentences.en: Well, it costs money.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它需要花钱。

sentences.en: It costs the taxpayers money, and that's a concern.
sentences.zh: 它花费纳税人的钱，这是一个令人担忧的问题。

sentences.en: In fact, the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities has estimated that Kentucky would have to raise taxes
sentences.zh: 事实上，预算与政策优先中心估计，肯塔基州将不得不增税

sentences.en: or cut other parts of its budget by $16 billion over 10 years in order to maintain Kentucky Medicaid the way it is, if the federal funding withered.
sentences.zh: 或者在10年内削减160亿美元的其他预算，以便在联邦资金枯竭的情况下维持肯塔基州医疗补助计划的现状。

sentences.en: And what about Kentucky residents you've spoken to who rely on this expanded Medicaid program under the Affordable Care Act?
sentences.zh: 那么你所交谈过的那些依赖《平价医疗法案》下这一扩大后的医疗补助计划的肯塔基州居民呢？

sentences.en: What do they say about their elected officials' determination to rein in the spending and potentially take action that might kick them off of Medicaid?
sentences.zh: 他们对民选官员控制支出并可能采取可能将他们踢出医疗补助计划的行动的决心有什么看法？

sentences.en: Well, obviously they're worried, but I have to say, Michael, that when people are really struggling to get by, they're not always paying such close attention to politics.
sentences.zh: 嗯，显然他们很担心，但我必须说，迈克尔，当人们真的在为生计挣扎时，他们并不总是那么关注政治。

sentences.en: I don't until something comes up, and then, you know, I really don't.
sentences.zh: 除非有什么事情发生，否则我不会关注，然后，你知道，我真的不怎么看。

sentences.en: It's so much that I just don't watch it.
sentences.zh: 太多了，我只是不看。

sentences.en: Well, what do you think of Senator McConnell being the author, the main driving force behind this Senate bill
sentences.zh: 那么，你如何看待麦康奈尔参议员作为这个参议院法案的作者和主要推动力，

sentences.en: that would cut the expansion of Medicaid under the Affordable Care Act that you now rely on for your lupus?
sentences.zh: 该法案将削减你现在因狼疮而依赖的《平价医疗法案》下的医疗补助扩张？

sentences.en: He's also lost my support, and he's no good for Kentucky.
sentences.zh: 他也失去了我的支持，他对肯塔基州没有好处。

sentences.en: Were you aware of how deeply involved he has been in this plan to roll back Medicaid?
sentences.zh: 你知道他参与这个撤回医疗补助计划的程度有多深吗？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And how did you learn about it?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么知道这件事的？

sentences.en: Ah, so, from the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 啊，是从《纽约时报》上看到的。

sentences.en: So, is what we're talking about voters who don't quite see the connection between the policy and the officials in Washington who they have elected?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们谈论的是那些不太能看出政策与他们在华盛顿选出的官员之间联系的选民吗？

sentences.en: Is that essentially what this boils down to?
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是问题的症结所在吗？

sentences.en: I think it is what it boils down to.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是问题的症结所在。

sentences.en: People in states like Kentucky have voted against their self-intereSt.
sentences.zh: 像肯塔基州这样的人们投票违背了自己的自身利益。

sentences.en: At the time, I don't recall him, that being part of his campaign.
sentences.zh: 当时，我不记得他把那作为他竞选活动的一部分。

sentences.en: I could be wrong, but I don't think it was.
sentences.zh: 我可能错了，但我不认为那是。

sentences.en: And I thought he would be good for it.
sentences.zh: 我以为他会对此有好处。

sentences.en: You know, he's been here, he knows about Kentucky, and he also knows the things about the poor people of Kentucky.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他一直在这里，他了解肯塔基州，他也了解肯塔基州穷人的情况。

sentences.en: He's definitely lost my support and my vote.
sentences.zh: 他绝对失去了我的支持和选票。

sentences.en: It'll be interesting to see what happens if these bills go through and they lose their health care and they wake up and say, wow, you know, we voted for this, and guess what?
sentences.zh: 如果这些法案通过，他们失去了医疗保健，然后醒悟过来说，哇，你知道，我们投票支持了这个，结果呢？

sentences.en: We don't have health insurance anymore.
sentences.zh: 我们再也没有医疗保险了，看看会发生什么，这会很有趣。

sentences.en: Kathy, what do you want to see for the future of Medicaid?
sentences.zh: 凯西，你希望医疗补助计划的未来是什么样的？

sentences.en: What do you want to see happen to it?
sentences.zh: 你希望它发生什么变化？

sentences.en: Because it is taking care of people that desperate,
sentences.zh: 因为它正在照顾那些绝望的人，

sentences.en: and without it, there's going to be very sick people.
sentences.zh: 没有它，会有非常多生病的人。

sentences.en: And so what do you want these two senators in Kentucky to do,
sentences.zh: 那么你希望肯塔基州的这两位参议员做什么，

sentences.en: Senator McConnell and Senator Paul?
sentences.zh: 麦康奈尔参议员和保罗参议员？

sentences.en: To fight for Kentucky, to fight to keep it the way it is, to keep Obamacare the way it is.
sentences.zh: 为肯塔基州而战，为保持现状而战，保持奥巴马医改的现状。

sentences.en: And just maybe little changes, not high-dollar changes.
sentences.zh: 也许只是做些小改动，而不是高成本的改动。

sentences.en: But I think it'd be best if they just leave it alone.
sentences.zh: 但我认为如果他们只是别管它，那是最好的。

sentences.en: Well, Kathy, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，凯西，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: I wish you the beSt.
sentences.zh: 祝你一切顺利。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: In your health and in your life.
sentences.zh: 在你的健康和生活中。

sentences.en: Thank you very much for your time.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你抽出时间。

sentences.en: Okay, and thank you.
sentences.zh: 好的，也谢谢你。

sentences.en: Okay, bye.
sentences.zh: 好的，再见。

sentences.en: The Senate debate over the future of Medicaid and American health care will resume when lawmakers return from their 10-day 4th of July recess.
sentences.zh: 关于医疗补助计划和美国医疗保健未来的参议院辩论将在立法者从为期10天的独立日休会回来后恢复。

sentences.en: Senator McConnell is still pushing for a vote to repeal and replace the Affordable Care Act.
sentences.zh: 麦康奈尔参议员仍在推动对废除并取代《平价医疗法案》进行投票。

sentences.en: But President Trump is now proposing that the Senate might consider abandoning that plan.
sentences.zh: 但特朗普总统现在提议参议院可以考虑放弃该计划。

sentences.en: If Republican senators are unable to pass what they are working on now, he tweeted over the weekend, they should immediately repeal and then replace at a later date.
sentences.zh: 如果共和党参议员无法通过他们目前正在做的事情，他在周末发推文说，他们应该立即废除，然后在以后的日期再进行取代。

sentences.en: That's a reversal from earlier this year.
sentences.zh: 这与今年早些时候的说法相反。

sentences.en: The Times reports that Senator McConnell and House Speaker Paul Ryan had both originally supported the repeal-now, replace-later approach
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》报道称，麦康奈尔参议员和众议院议长保罗·瑞安最初都支持“先废除，后取代”的方法，

sentences.en: until President Trump publicly demanded that they be done together after his election in January.
sentences.zh: 直到特朗普总统在1月当选后公开要求将两者同时进行。

sentences.en: It'll be repeal and replace.
sentences.zh: 这将是废除并取代。

sentences.en: It will be essentially simultaneously.
sentences.zh: 基本上会是同时进行。

sentences.en: It will be various segments, you understand, but will most likely be on the same day or the same week, but probably the same day.
sentences.zh: 这将是不同的部分，你明白，但很可能是在同一天或同一周，但很可能是在同一天。

sentences.en: Could be the same hour.
sentences.zh: 可能是同一个小时。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周在《Wirecutter秀》上，我们正准备为假期接待客人。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人感到宾至如归的建议。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是那种需要完全遮光才能睡觉的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they black out to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否会昏睡过去。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是指，他们需要什么样的光线环境？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为那是一件非常具体的事情。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》应用程序或你喜欢的任何地方收听《Wirecutter秀》。
